title: Van Rysel RCR-F Review - An Affordable Aero Bike?

takeaways.text: Electronic groupsets only; the integrated computer mount is plastic and wobbled with a large computer and light, and the bar is wider than he would like.
In Cyclingnews' tunnel it was the second-fastest bike tested as a bike alone but mid-table with a rider, about 0.6 W slower than the RCR Pro; swapping the stock Swiss Side wheels cost 1.6 W.
The front end is low (7 mm below an equivalent Tarmac) and stiff; with deep wheels and a 26 mm front tire it felt harsh on long rides, and 42 cm bars offset the aero gain.
Power transfer feels excellent and it suits short punchy climbs, but it is heavy on long ascents: about 8.5 kg for the 105 build and about 8 kg in Ultegra spec; 30 mm tires improved handling.
He finds it about £400 dearer than an equivalent Canyon Aeroad, a hard sell on value.

disclosure: Publication review with wind-tunnel testing; the bike shown is the Ultegra-spec RCR-F, and the reviewer also references the 105-spec bike he tested earlier on the same frame.
summary: Cyclingnews' ride and wind-tunnel review of the Van Rysel RCR-F aero bike.
